newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL HAS RECORD Q1, NEAR EXPECTATIONS - CEO.
newsitem.headline: MOL HAS RECORD Q1, NEAR EXPECTATIONS - CEO.

text.p: Hungarian oil and gas company Magyar Olaj- es Gazipari Rt (MOL) on Tuesday reported a 51 percent growth in its IAS group net income for the first three months of 1997, making the group's best quarter.

MOL's net income in the first quarter of the year rose to 12.737 billion forints from 8.420 billion forints in the same period of last year, while its net sales grew to 169.907 billion from 123.039 billion.

"These results are broadly in line with our expectations and represent record quarterly earnings in the history of our company," Zoltan Mandoki, MOL's Chief Executive Officer said in MOL's earnings report.
The result was close to a Reuters survey of six analysts and traders on Friday which showed that the average of the market's expectation of MOL's net income was 13 billion.

MOL's operating profit rose to 20.707 billion forints in the first three months of the year, up from 14.302 billion in the same period of last year, with a strong contribution from its exploration and production (E&P) division.
The operating profit for E&P increased to 17.1 billion forints and was 1.3 billion forints for refining and marketing.

"The results of our E&P division was particularly robust on the back of reducing but still higher crude oil and LPG (liquefied petroleum gas) prices and a beneficial reducing impact on gas imports resulting from unseasonably mild January and February weather," Mandoki said.

"Although our domestic downstream business continued to be affected by the macro-economic environment, we strengthened our wholesale position despite increasing competition and first signs of recovery are clearly visible."
MOL strengthened its leading market shares in motoric gasoline to 86 percent, up nine percent from the first quarter of 1996, and in gas and heating oils to 89 percent, up three percent.
Its wholesale market share of bitumens and lubricants was unchanged at 98 percent and 65 percent, respectively, while its market share plunged to 62 percent from 82 percent in fuel oils, MOL said.
MOL's strongest quarter has traditionally been the first three months of the year, the company said, but Mandoki expressed hopes that the growth in shareholder value could be maintained.
"The strong improvement in the group's financial performance in its traditionally strongest quarter reflects further encouraging signs that our business strategy is delivering results," Mandoki said.

"I am very confident that we are well positioned to take advantage of further opportunities which exist to expand our business and further improve the company's financial performance to deliver sustained growth in shareholder value...".
